redundancy

/rih-DUHN-duhn-see/ - the stress falls on DUHN · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Redundancy means needless repetition or duplication.

The twins' chore board lists 'feed the dog' under both names — a redundancy the dog exploits nightly for second dinners.

Example

The homeowners' welcome packet holds three letters, each explaining the same parking rule in nearly the same words. New neighbors read the first, skim the second, and recycle the third unopened. When the board finally merged them to cut the redundancy, not one fact was lost — because two of the three letters had never carried one.

Redundancy names repetition that adds nothing. The letters weren't wordy — each was short and clear; the problem was that the packet said the same thing three times, and twice for free. Where a repeat serves no purpose, redundancy is the editor's word for it.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

duplication: Duplication is a second copy of something that already exists — and it can even be deliberate: the backup file, the spare form in the drawer. Redundancy is duplication judged and found useless, the repeat that serves no purpose. Every redundancy contains a duplicate; only the pointless duplicate earns the name redundancy.

wordiness: Wordiness wraps a real point in more words than it needs — the message survives, buried under throat-clearing and ornament. Redundancy is a different flaw: the point is made, then made again for free. Wordy writing says one thing slowly; redundancy says the same thing twice.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

economy: of words: each one earning its place, nothing said twice

brevity: shortness itself, however it was achieved

Where it sits · how little the repetition earns its place — restatement → redundancy → padding

restatement vs. redundancy: A restatement repeats on purpose — to clarify or drive a point home; redundancy is the repeat that earns nothing.

padding vs. redundancy: Padding sits past redundancy on the editor's frown scale: not just the same thing twice, but bulk shoveled in purely to lengthen.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — red-

Prefix — red-: again, back (re- before a vowel)

Root — und-

Root — und-: wave (Latin unda)

Suffix — -ancy

Suffix — -ancy: state of

Put it together

Put it together: Red- (again — the form re- takes before a vowel) + und- (wave, Latin unda) + -ancy = the state of waving back again. Latin redundare pictured water rushing back over the brim — overflow. A redundancy is language doing what the flood does: coming round again where once was already plenty.

Use the root in a new word: surround

Use the root in a new word: surround: By dusk the floodwater had surrounded the farmhouse, lapping at all four sides.

Word Choice

neutral / editorial

Redundancy is the repeat that earns nothing — the editor's flag, cousin to superfluous (a unit-mate: beyond need, whether or not repeated). One caution before you wield it: engineers use redundancy approvingly — backup pumps, twin generators — where a second copy is the whole point. This unit's sense is the needless kind: said once already, said again for free.
